subtitle: Read it later, on your own server
description:
Shelf keeps the articles you mean to read. Paste a link, click the Save to Shelf button in your browser, share from your phone, or ask Claude to save something it found. Shelf fetches the page on your server and keeps a clean copy: the article's words and pictures, without the ads and pop-ups, so it's still there when the site changes.

The reader is set in Newsreader, a typeface made for reading on screens, in the size and width you like, on white or a paper tone, in light or dark. Shelf keeps your place and takes you back to it on any device. Select words to highlight them or add a note; your highlights gather in one place and find their spot again if the article is fetched afresh. Share one by link, with a preview card set in the reader’s typefaces.

A few highlights come back each day in a daily review, one at a time on paper: keep one in mind and it waits a while, favourite it and it returns more often, send it away for good, add a note or a tag, and keep a streak. Bring in your Kindle's clippings and your Readwise highlights, or type in passages from a book on paper; each book gets its cover and its highlights in order. Take everything with you as Markdown for Obsidian or Notion, or as a CSV Readwise can read.

Follow blogs, newsletters with a feed and YouTube channels: new posts gather in the Feed, apart from your reading list, and a swipe saves the ones worth reading. Videos play right in the reader. Bring your feeds from any reader as OPML.

Ask for a three-point summary from your server's AI, or listen: your device reads the article aloud, a sentence at a time, and the page follows along. Search finds words inside the articles and your highlights, not only in titles.

Bring your links from Pocket, Instapaper, Readwise Reader or a bookmarks file. Connect Shelf to Claude and it can list, read and search your shelf, quote your highlights and save links for you.

It feels like an app: frosted bars that stay put, the article beside the list on a desk and sliding over it on a phone, swipes to archive and favourite, keys for everything on a desk, and articles that read offline.
whatsNew: The Feed: follow sites, newsletters with a feed and YouTube channels, read what's new, and swipe to save the best to your reading list. OPML in and out, videos in the reader, and Claude can see your Feed too. On a phone the Feed has its own tab, and Favourites is a chip on the reading list.

The Feed on a phone: unseen posts from NASA Image of the Day and The Public Domain Review with their pictures, and the Feed tab
The daily review: a favourited passage from Pride and Prejudice on paper, with its cover, a note and its Kindle location, and Next
Thoreau's Walking in the reader, set in Newsreader, with a highlighted passage
The Highlights page: today's review done with a one-day streak, chips for favourites, books and articles, and highlights from The Elements of Style and North of Boston under their covers
Walden from a Kindle as a notebook on Shelf: four highlights in book order with their locations and notes, and buttons to review it or add a highlight
Text settings over the article on a paper tone: Newsreader or Inter, eight sizes, plain or paper
A shared highlight from Thoreau's Walking as anyone with the link sees it: the words, the article and who highlighted them, and how to get your own Shelf
The Great Wave off Kanagawa in the reader in dark mode, with Hokusai's print and its caption
The daily review in dark mode: a line from Walden with a note about using it as an epigraph
Save from anywhere: the Save to Shelf bookmark, Android's share sheet, the iPhone, and Shelf's address for adding it to Claude as a connector
